nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Eco-friendly construction materials|Biodegradable and recyclable insulation_qna_000
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: What are the two parts of SPL identified in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The carbon-rich part of SPL is called first cut, while the refractory and insulation materials are referred to as second cut.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Eco-friendly construction materials|Biodegradable and recyclable insulation_qna_001
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What is the primary purpose of the study on bio-based insulation materials?
nodes.answer: The primary purpose is to provide comprehensive environmental information on bio-based thermal insulation materials to empower professionals in making informed decisions and promoting their selection.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Eco-friendly construction materials|Biodegradable and recyclable insulation_qna_002
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What data was collected to create a Life Cycle Inventory (LCI) for the insulation materials?
nodes.answer: Data on manufacturing, use, recyclability, and technical performance of eleven commercially available natural insulation materials was collected.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Eco-friendly construction materials|Biodegradable and recyclable insulation_qna_003
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How does the study aim to compare bio-based insulation materials to non-bio-based ones?
nodes.answer: The study compares them by ranking the thirteen environmental impact categories in EN 15804(2013) + A2(2019) to provide an overview of their potential benefits and burdens.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Eco-friendly construction materials|Biodegradable and recyclable insulation_qna_004
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What materials were found to have the lowest environmental impact in the scenario analysis?
nodes.answer: Recycled cotton and hemp fibre insulation were found to have the lowest impact across all categories.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Eco-friendly construction materials|Biodegradable and recyclable insulation_qna_005
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What aspect of recycled textile insulation was highlighted by the dynamic LCIA?
nodes.answer: The dynamic LCIA indicated that recycled textile insulation has the lowest impact in both short-term and long-term scenarios, regardless of the end-of-life option chosen.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Eco-friendly construction materials|Biodegradable and recyclable insulation_qna_006
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What are the main advantages of bio-based insulation materials compared to traditional fossil-based insulations?
nodes.answer: Bio-based insulation materials use renewable resources, can store carbon when produced under environment-friendly practices, and, if not recyclable, can sometimes be used for soil conditioning.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Eco-friendly construction materials|Biodegradable and recyclable insulation_qna_007
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What studies are mentioned that have analyzed the environmental impact of bio-based insulation materials?
nodes.answer: Several studies including those by Schmidt et al. (2004a; 2004b), Murphy and Norton (2008), Pargana et al. (2014), Schulte et al. (2021), and Carcassi et al. (2022) have found lower environmental impacts for some bio-based materials.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Eco-friendly construction materials|Biodegradable and recyclable insulation_qna_008
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: Can bio-based insulation materials be recycled?
nodes.answer: Bio-based insulation materials can sometimes be used for soil conditioning if they are not recyclable.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Eco-friendly construction materials|Biodegradable and recyclable insulation_qna_009
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What is the main focus of the studies conducted by Cascione et al. (2022a, b) and Carcassi et al. (2022)?
nodes.answer: The main focus of the studies is to investigate the environmental impacts of novel bio-based insulation materials using Global Warming Potential (GWP100) as the primary indicator.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Eco-friendly construction materials|Biodegradable and recyclable insulation_qna_010
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What was the focus of the studies by Carcassi et al. (2022) and Hawkins et al. (2021)?
nodes.answer: The focus of the studies was to demonstrate the significant potential of bio-based insulation to offset carbon emissions and highlight the advantages of bio-based materials based on specific products.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Eco-friendly construction materials|Biodegradable and recyclable insulation_qna_011
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How can wool fibres be repurposed in industries?
nodes.answer: Wool fibres can be repurposed in industries for thermal and acoustic insulation purposes, as well as in pads for soaking up oil spills, showcasing the versatility and sustainability of wool in various applications.
